sections.h2: Where to go for property tax
sections.html:
The Assessor and the Auditor/Treasurer both work out of the Itasca County Courthouse, 123 NE 4th Street, Grand Rapids, MN 55744, with weekday hours ending at 4:30 p.m. The Auditor/Treasurer is on the second floor. Call the Assessor at 218-327-2861 and the Treasurer at 218-327-2860.

The Assessor finds, lists and values every taxable parcel, works out net tax capacity by property class, mails owners their value and classification, and runs the local and county boards of equalization. The Auditor/Treasurer sends out statements and takes payment.

Itasca is big lake-and-forest country in the Iron Range region, with Grand Rapids as the seat. It is the third-largest Minnesota county by area, with 2,668 square miles of land, and it holds more than 1,400 lakes, including Winnibigoshish, Pokegama, Deer and Bowstring. The July 2025 estimate is 45,404 residents, only 0.9% above 2020.

There are 26,005 housing units, and 83.0% of occupied homes are owned. The median owner-occupied home is worth $225,200. The 2020 census found 25.2% of housing units vacant, a sign of how many cabins and seasonal places are in the mix. That matters when you list, because a lake property or a seasonal home is taxed under a different class than a house lived in all year.

The Assessor's office handles valuation for every taxable parcel in the county, so a seller in a far-flung township such as Bigfork, Marcell or Wawina still begins at the courthouse in Grand Rapids for value and classification questions. Where a city assessor also works in your area, the county assessor passes a copy of any petition to that authority, so ask which office issued your notice.

A residential bill splits into May 15 and October 15 payments. Resorts, manufactured homes and agricultural land keep their own dates, and a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday moves any date to the next business day.

Itasca County payment due dates
Due dateTax type
May 15Real property, first half (or whole bill if $100 or less)
May 31Real property, resorts, first half
August 31Manufactured homes, first half (or whole bill if $50 or less)
October 15Real property, second half
November 15Agricultural real property and manufactured homes, second half

Personal property and severed mineral interest taxes come due along with the real property tax.

sections.h2: How to pay an Itasca County tax bill
sections.html:
You can pay by mail, online, by phone or at the office, where cash, check and debit or credit card are taken. A mailed check needs a postmark no later than the due date.

  • Cards carry a 2.25% service fee with a $1.00 minimum.
  • An e-check through MuniciPay costs a flat $1.00 per transaction under $100,000.
  • Phone payments go through 218-535-7880 and need the Property ID Number from the top left of the statement.
  • Online and phone payments take one to two business days to post.

Automatic payment enrollment is free, with the same $1.00 ACH fee. If your taxes are paid from a mortgage escrow, the statement carries a note not to pay, and any change of escrow agent has to come from the escrow company to the Auditor/Treasurer.

An installment that goes unpaid draws 2% on a homestead and 4% on anything else, under Minnesota Statutes section 279.01. The same step repeats on the first of the next month, then one percent more is added each month through December.

The caps are 8% for homestead and 12% for nonhomestead property. Agricultural homestead and certain rural land get relief on the second half only: no penalty if it is paid by November 15. The county treasurer may also waive a penalty once when a mailed payment is postmarked within one business day of the due date. Cabins and seasonal recreational property that are not used commercially pay the homestead penalty rates, which counts for a lot in a county with this many lake properties.

Talk to the Assessor first, then take it to the local board in your city or township, then the county board. The Assessor treats this review as the first stage of an appeal, and appears in tax court when needed.

If you still disagree, Minnesota Statutes section 278.01 allows a district court petition, served on the county auditor and filed with the court administrator no later than April 30 of the tax-payable year. A Tax Court appeal is open between the day the valuation notice arrives and May 1. If a change in value or class reaches you only after February 28, you have 60 days from the day the notice was mailed.

Board schedules change from year to year, so call 218-327-2861 for the current meeting dates.

Get a current statement or payoff from the Auditor/Treasurer for your parcel, and confirm whether the first and second halves of the current year are both paid. The county has its own parcel information system and an online statement lookup.

A house at a lake, on forest land or in a township far from Grand Rapids may carry special assessments, so confirm every line with the county office before you set a closing date. For an inherited, empty or delinquent property, bring the parcel number and latest statement and ask what is owed through the date you expect to close. Paying that figure at the table is what lets the deed move forward, and a cash sale does not skip it.

faqs.q: When is the Itasca County first half due?
faqs.a: May 15 for regular real property. Resorts have until May 31 for the first half, and weekend or holiday dates roll forward.

faqs.q: What is the card fee for paying Itasca County taxes?
faqs.a: 2.25% of the payment, with a $1.00 minimum. An e-check through the county's online service is a flat $1.00 per transaction under $100,000.

faqs.q: Where is the Itasca County Assessor?
faqs.a: In the Itasca County Courthouse at 123 NE 4th Street, Grand Rapids, MN 55744. Weekday hours run to 4:30 p.m., and the phone is 218-327-2861.

faqs.q: When is the court deadline to contest an Itasca County tax?
faqs.a: April 30 of the tax-payable year for a district court petition under Minnesota Statutes section 278.01. A Tax Court appeal can begin earlier, between the valuation notice and May 1.

faqs.q: Do manufactured homes in Itasca County follow the same calendar?
faqs.a: No. Manufactured homes pay the first half August 31 (or the whole bill if it is $50 or less) and the remainder November 15.
